note: Round 1051: real career shapes and the ballot the real Hall gave them, for section 18 of scripts/simCareerHall.mjs. Scripts side only: nothing in src or in shipped copy names a real player. Every value was read off a page fetched on the read date, and each source records the words the page said. A fact that could not be two sourced from two different publishers (neither a wiki) is not here: a thin table is honest, a padded one is not.

rule: FAMILIES. Every standout family of the calibration 2 tables that calibration 1 did not read and that has an official published career list: NBA rebounds and assists; NFL receptions, receiving touchdowns, interceptions, sacks and field goals; MLB saves and steals; NHL goals and assists.
NO FAMILY ANCHORS for tackles (the league keeps no official career list), passes defensed and forced fumbles (not counted the same way across eras), or holds (not an official statistic).

WHO. For each family, the first five names in the published career list's own order who are retired, whose last season is 2015 or earlier (so at least five classes have judged them), and who are not skipped below.

BASEBALL. The writers' ballot runs ten years, so a man whose last season is 2011 to 2015 and who is not yet inducted would be recorded as pending and kept out of every count. A man the writers dropped under five percent is never, whatever the year. A man already inducted is settled.

TWO OF EACH. If a sport then holds fewer than two anchors of any ballot kind (first, later, never), the next names down the same lists are added, one list at a time in the order above, until it holds two.

SKIPPED, each recorded with its reason: a ban or a scandal that decided his case; a career or part of a stat line in a league the engine does not model; a position change that splits his line; a career that ended before the awards the engine counts were given.

COUNTS. Awards are the engine's own counts and nothing else. A ring is a league title won as a player. An All-Star count is seasons selected, never games. NBA: titles, MVPs, Finals MVPs, All-NBA selections of any team. NFL: titles, first team AP All-Pro selections, and the AP MVP for QB, RB, WR, TE and K but the AP Defensive Player of the Year for LB, CB and EDGE. MLB: World Series titles, All-Star seasons, and MVPs for hitters but Cy Young Awards for pitchers. NHL: Stanley Cups, Conn Smythes, All-Star Game selections, and the Hart for forwards, the Norris for defencemen, the Vezina for goalies.

HOCKEY'S ALL-STAR COUNT, corrected 2026-10-08 before any hockey anchor was scored: the engine's own count is the season-end First and Second All-Star Team, never the All-Star Game (src/lib/nhlMyCareer.ts where the nod is drawn: twelve players make it a year, six positions across two teams), and awards are the engine's own counts and nothing else. So a hockey anchor's allStars is his First plus Second All-Star Team seasons, which two publishers list season by season. The All-Star Game line in COUNTS above is superseded for hockey.

TOTALS. Regular season only, every family the engine's season line records for the position. A total that could not be two sourced is null with its reason, and the harness reads it as zero and says so.

BALLOT. Judged on the ballot the engine models (the writers' ballot in baseball, the modern era vote in football, the North American committee in basketball, the player category in hockey). first: the first class he was eligible for took him. later: a later class of that same ballot took him. never: it has not as of the read date. A man a veterans or era committee put in after the main ballot passed on him is never with route committee, and is printed apart, outside every count.

TWO READINGS, both printed. raw: the real line as it is, at real scale, with no conversion constant. books: for an anchor taken off a family list whose position carries that family as a standout, the engine career with that family's total set to the calibration 2 table's to mark for his position, every other total multiplied by the same factor (the to mark over his real total, rounded), his awards raw, his seasons raw but no more than the sport's hard stop (19 NFL, 21 NBA, 21 MLB, 22 NHL). A top five career on the real list is a top of the books career by the standout's own definition, and that is all the rule claims. An anchor whose position does not carry his family as a standout, and a name added from lower down a list only to reach two of each ballot, is read raw only and printed apart.
ADDED 2026-10-08, before any basketball, football or hockey anchor was scored (baseball's ten rows are untouched by every line below).

PAIRS. A row is a man on a family list. A man in the first five of two lists is two rows that share one set of sources (the second row names the first in sameAs), because the books reading differs by family. The counts of 8 a sport and two of each ballot are counts of men, never of rows.

TWO OF EACH, how the walk down goes. While a later is missing, every eligible name is added in the list's order, since the list page cannot tell a first from a later. While only a never is missing, a name the list page itself marks as a Hall of Famer is passed over. Names added this way are read raw only.

OTHER LEAGUES, read narrowly. A man is skipped when the listed total itself mixes in another league's numbers (the combined NBA and ABA lists), when he played seasons in another major league after his first season in this one, or when he was inducted and then played on. A season in another league before his first season here does not skip him: the list, his line and his Hall case are this league's.

AWARDS THAT CAME LATE. A man is skipped when his last season is before the first year a count the engine reads for his position was given (the AP Defensive Player of the Year from 1971 for a defender; the Finals MVP from 1969). A career that only began before that year stays in.

POSITIONS. The engine's CB is its only defensive back, so a real corner or safety is read at CB. Its EDGE is every pass rusher on the sack list, defensive end or outside linebacker. In basketball and hockey a man is read at the first position his stat line's publisher lists for him, mapped to the engine's five.

FIRST ELIGIBLE CLASS outside baseball. Basketball, football and hockey publish no ballot, so a man's first eligible class is his last season plus that Hall's waiting rule (the eligibility block, two sourced once per sport), and first, later or never follows by arithmetic from his two sourced class. Where a page says in words that he went in his first eligible year, the words are recorded too.

sportsNotBuilt.nfl: not built: the awards group cannot be two sourced. The count the rule asks for is first team AP All-Pro selections, and the one publisher read that separates the AP's team is Pro Football Reference (it refuses a fetch and is readable only through its archived pages). The Hall's own pages count first team All-Pro seasons of every selector and so disagree by rule (for the receptions leader: named first-team All-Pro 11 consecutive seasons, against ten AP first teams). The stat lines (nfl.com) and the classes (profootballhof.com) can be read. The lead decides: one publisher for football's awards, a count by any selector, or football unjudged.

decisions.counts: Halved: raw 9 > 8 and 6 > 5 of 9, books 8 > 7 and 5 > 4 of 8. Dropped: raw 9 > 8 and 6 > 5 of 9, books 4 > 4 and 3 > 3 of 4 (no reliever has a books reading any more).

decisions.why: mlb-saves-4 sits at 469 on hardware and seasons alone (four All-Star seasons, 21 seasons), 31 under the line. The base (saves per 8, holds per 12, strikeouts per 40) put him in at 546 in the raw reading; halved (per 16, 24 and 80) he was still in at 508, by 8.
decisions.counts: Base whole: raw 9 > 8 and 6 > 5 of 9. Halved: raw 9 > 8 and 6 > 5. Dropped: raw 9 > 9 and 6 > 6, books 4 > 4 and 3 > 3 of 4.

measured.note: The agreement on calibration 2, as the harness printed it when the sport was built, and what each agreement control can reach: realNotFirstInBooks is the count of real never or later anchors with a books reading (standoutbig needs one), pushAlone the count that agree on 2 only because of the push (standoutgone needs more than two). The harness holds all of it to what it computes today. A row is a man on a list, so basketball's n of 14 is 14 men and hockey's 17 is 16 men.

nba.read: Calibration 1 agreed just as often (raw 12 and 12 of 14, books 10 and 10 of 10): nine of the ten list men are in on hardware either way. The one real never with a books reading (nba-ast-4) stays out on calibration 2 at 486 against a line of 500, so the full push at point guard holds, by 14 points. No decision. The two real laters (raw only) are out on both calibrations: the engine's line was set for careers half again as long.

nhl.read: Calibration 1 agreed on raw 12 and 11 of 17 and on books 7 and 7 of 10. The push puts three real first ballot men in who were out on 1 (nhl-goals-3, nhl-goals-5, nhl-assists-2). No decision. Every list man here went straight in, so nothing in hockey can say the push is too big: the harness prints that, and standoutbig refuses to run here.
